title: What Is Prayer?
imageAlt: A simple way to begin: Worship — Tell God who He is. Thank Him for what He has done. Fellowship — Be still. Read a short passage. Listen for His voice. Petition — Tell Him your needs with thanksgiving, not anxiety. JOY — Pray for others by name. Then bring yourself last.

title: Why Pray?
imageAlt: Twelve reasons to pray: He invites you, listens, answers, draws near, blesses, meets needs, protects, gives wisdom, shapes you, builds His kingdom, makes His presence known, and is worthy.

title: A.C.T.S. of Prayer
imageAlt: A.C.T.S.: Adoration — Praise the Father for who He is. Confession — Agree with God about sin — and about who you are in Christ. Thanksgiving — Thank Him for forgiveness, guidance, provision, and protection. Supplication — Ask for help, and intercede for others.

title: Prayers in the Bible
imageAlt: Examples across Scripture: Hannah — 1 Samuel 1–2. David — Psalm 51. Solomon — 1 Kings 8. Jehoshaphat — 2 Chronicles 20. Jonah — Jonah 2. Daniel — Daniel 9.

title: Prayer and Fasting
imageAlt: Why fast? Seek God — Use hunger as a call to prayer, not as a way to earn favor. Repent — Fasting often accompanies grief over sin and a return to the Lord. Ask for help — God’s people have fasted in crisis, danger, and need. Listen — Set aside noise and appetite so you can hear His voice. Serve His mission — The early church fasted when they sent workers and sought direction.

title: My Prayer List
imageAlt: Prayer list groups: My family and friends — the people closest to your daily life. My church and special ministries — pastors, workers, and the work of the gospel. My community, state, and nation — leaders, schools, neighbors, and public life. Believers around the world — the church in other places, including those under pressure. Other prayers of intercession — names and needs that do not fit the groups above. Help me with my needs, Lord — your own concerns, brought last — not forgotten.
